title: Texas DPS - Flock Cameras in Smith County, Tyler TX

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Context: Please Read--In 2025 Texas DPS submitted a map of Texas to MVCPA with proposed Flock camera locations, 1,183 in total. The map is pictured, in reporting done by the Texas Tribune following a successful open records request, at the following hyperlink: https://i0.wp.com/www.texastribune.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Flock-DPS-Map.jpg?resize=2000%2C1500&ssl=1 ("After Abbott’s order limiting Flock cameras, DPS to continue using its vast surveillance network", Texas Tribune, Sep 4 2026, URL: https://www.texastribune.org/2026/09/04/texas-flock-cameras-dps-network-search-abbott/ )

Accordingly, I request the following:

A. Current, recent map, or photograph of map, from year 2026, newest date available, of proposed DPS Flock camera locations centering on Smith County, Texas. Electronic formats that would be acceptable would include: .pdf, .jpg, .png, etc. This is a request for a map or other geographical representation of DPS Flock Cameras only in Smith County. A map within Flock's software program is produced in following manner: initialize Flock dashboard/application, Select 'Map' option, ensure Smith County, Texas is visible and zoomed into, and screenshot the map, or print the result (to pdf or other method).
B.  Current, recent map, or photograph of map, from year 2026, newest date available, of active or pending DPS Flock camera locations centering on Smith County, Texas.  Electronic formats that would be acceptable would include: .pdf, .jpg, .png, etc. This is a request for a map or other geographical representation of DPS Flock Cameras only in Smith County. A map within Flock's software program is produced in following manner: initialize Flock dashboard/application, Select 'Map' option, ensure Smith County, Texas is visible and zoomed into,  and screenshot the map, or print the result (to pdf or other method).
C.  Current, recent text list, spreadsheet, pdf document, etc; from year 2026, newest date available, of active, pending and proposed DPS Flock camera locations including only Smith County, Texas. This document should include coordinates or exact location of cameras, plus show general information such as camera make or model. Electronic formats that would be acceptable would include: .pdf, .jpg, .png, .xls, .doc, json, etc. This is a request for materials relating to DPS Flock Cameras only in Smith County.

D. In the event that you will NOT release the responsive materials for any reason, (Items A-C), including but not limited to any of the following broad justifications: "trade secret", "active criminal investigation", "attorney general", "no responsive documents", "unable to meet deadline", "sent to Flock for review", etc;  I request POs (purchase orders), receipts, payment requests, invoices, financial documents, approval documents, highway right-of-way documents (that DPS would have necessarily submitted to TxDOT to obtain site approval for emplacement of Flock cameras), site surveys, payment stubs, payment records, installation records for ALL DPS proposed, pending or existing Flock ALPR cameras in Smith County, Texas. These cameras are in visible, prominent public locations and are shared widely. I will clarify if necessary on Item D to reduce the size of this portion of request if there is large amount of material. I am seeking material relating to roughly 12 Flock cameras/ camera sites in Smith County. Please release material for Item D as soon as possible to avoid further unnecessary delays. Produce easily available, or easily releasable material first.

Other stipulations and qualifiers:
This is not a request to create/generate new material. The Texas AG's office states in 2026 Public Information Act handbook: "A request for public information that requires a governmental body to program or manipulate existing data is not considered a request for the creation of new information." (source:https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/sites/default/files/files/divisions/open-government/PIA-Handbook-2026.pdf , pg 29 quoting/citing: Fish v. Dallas Indep. Sch. Dist., 31 S.W.3d 678, 681-82 (Tex. App.—Eastland 2000, pet. denied); see Gov’t Code § 552.231; Attorney General Opinion H-90 (1973); Open Records Decision Nos. 452 at 2-3 (1986), 87 (1975) ).  This is an open records request that seeks manipulation or processing of preexisting data or electronic media. I note that previously DPS released a statewide map, showing very nearly the exact location of each camera--discernible by referencing landmarks and streets, so producing a localized map and associated documentation should not present any issue.

Note: visual inspection of the hyperlinked 2025 dated map for whole state of Texas, focusing on Smith County only, reveals approximately 12 distinct "pins" which would represent 12 proposed, pending or existing Flock cameras that would be operated by Texas DPS. This includes approx. 6 on or adjacent to Loop 49 tollroad, and approximately 5 that appear to be on or adjacent to Loop 323 in the northern half of Tyler, Texas. Thus, there should be more current maps that align with this already public information of location records, or in event you fail to produce maps, documentation for approximately 12 DPS Flock camera sites in Smith County, primarily in or near the City of Tyler. To be clear if there are more than 12 cameras in Smith County, I want that material too.

In event of proposed redaction, I need advance notice, and a valid reason given; redaction may be accepted or rejected. May also reserve right to amend request to make it easier to complete request. Notice is also needed if request timeline extends beyond ten business days, or if AG ruling is sought. If there is large number of documents, please notify so request can be amended or clarified.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Piney Woods ALPR
